papers.title: Bose-Einstein condensate in a shell: nonlinear modes and symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: The state of a quantum particle confined to a spherical surface is commonly described using spherical harmonics, which play a crucial role in solving many scientific problems featuring spherical symmetry. A mean-field description of a system of many interacting quantum particles confined to a spherical shell naturally leads to nonlinear generalizations of spherical harmonics. In this study, we analyze the emergence of such nonlinear modes in a shell-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with both repulsive and attractive two-particle interactions. We find several classes of nonlinear modes. The first kind is an analytical continuation of a single spherical harmonic or their superposition for nonvanishing atom-atom interaction. Some of these solutions have planar counterparts in the form of Townes solitons and Townes vortices, which either appear stable even in the case of attractive interactions or can be stabilized by three-particle interactions. The second kind originate from symmetry-breaking bifurcations in the case of a repulsive interaction, and therefore have no linear counterparts. Moreover, we demonstrate the existence of a breathing dynamics that oscillates primarily between an unstable soliton and a stable vortex necklace state. Our findings show that the physics of nonlinear matter waves on curved geometries differs substantially from that in planar systems, suggesting the feasibility of observing these unconventional wave patterns experimentally.

papers.title: Phase-Sensitive Validation of Reduced-Order Nonlinear Mechanical Models with Dynamic Readout
papers.abstract: Reduced-order models of nonlinear structures are often evaluated using mechanical response errors, while the signals of interest may also pass through dynamic readout channels that modify their amplitudes and phases. We develop an offline validation framework that distinguishes mechanical source error, readout-model prediction error, and physical distortion of a normalized two-component modal state. We couple a Galerkin reduced source to two calibrated resonant channels and evaluate modal amplitudes, relative phase, and state fidelity using consistent complex coefficients. For the linear readout model, an exact output-error decomposition distinguishes source and interface modeling contributions, while a two-channel identity relates differential channel transfer to normalized-state distortion. For the ten-mass nonlinear lattice, the two-mode source and coupled-output errors over the two-resonance interface band are $3.069 \times 10^{-2}$ and $2.448 \times 10^{-2}$. At $F_0=0.04$, the relative-phase mean absolute error increases from $9.82 \times 10^{-3}$ rad for the linear interface to $1.74 \times 10^{-2}$ rad for the nonlinear interface. At the strongest forcing, a four-coordinate proper orthogonal decomposition model gives a source error of $2.05 \times 10^{-2}$, compared with $8.03 \times 10^{-2}$ for four linear modes on the same held-out test set. The noise analysis shows that accurate in-band output prediction can coexist with substantial parameter error, while a constrained linear approximation of nonlinear readout data produces a substantial residual. We use these findings to assess reduced-model adequacy for the specified outputs, forcing levels, and validation frequencies.

papers.title: Integrable turbulence and statistical properties of chaotic wave fields in the complex modified Korteweg-de Vries equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates integrable turbulence and the mechanism for generating rogue waves in the complex modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV) equation through numerical simulations and statistical analysis. We solve the Lax pair eigenvalue problem using the Fourier collocation method and establish a correspondence among solitons, breathers, and rogue waves on the spectral plane. We generate chaotic wave fields by simulating the complex mKdV equation using the split-step Fourier method, starting from a plane wave with superimposed random noise. We analyze the effects of the standard deviation \(\mu\) and the correlation length \(L_c\). The results show that increasing \(\mu\) drives a transition from breather turbulence to soliton turbulence, increasing the probability of rogue-wave generation.In contrast, \(L_c\) primarily influences the spatial scale of the structures. As the constant background of the complex mKdV equation is modulationally stable, its integrable turbulence does not depend on modulational instability. Compared with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation under identical initial conditions, the complex mKdV equation attains comparable amplitudes under strong perturbations, but exhibits a higher spatial gradient. This suggests that third-order dispersion and derivative nonlinearity alter the excitation mechanism and steepen the waveform.

papers.title: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
papers.abstract: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength \epsilon and map parameter \omega, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.
